entities.name: BRCA1
observations: Myocardial BRCA1 protein expression was measured by semiquantitative immunohistochemistry in an IDCM explant study.

In 10 men with end-stage IDCM, cardiocyte staining was significantly higher and spatially heterogeneous versus 10 male donor controls; hypertrophied cardiocytes stained intensely while typical cardiomyopathic cardiocytes stained weakly.
The observed pattern was interpreted as reflecting adverse myocardial remodeling, but the cross-sectional study did not establish causality or future predictive value.

entities.name: Idiopathic Dilated Cardiomyopathy
observations: The direct BRCA1 study examined explanted myocardium from 10 men with end-stage idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy undergoing transplantation.
No retrieved primary study demonstrated that BRCA1 predicts serial left-ventricular reverse remodeling, myocardial fibrosis burden, or clinical outcomes in IDCM.

entities.name: PMID:27496484
observations: BRCA1 Reflects Myocardial Adverse Remodeling in Idiopathic Dilated Cardiomyopathy; Transplantation Proceedings, 2016.
Case-control myocardial immunohistochemistry study: 10 male IDCM transplant recipients versus 10 male cerebral-death donor controls.
The study supports BRCA1 expression as an end-stage tissue correlate of adverse remodeling, not as a validated longitudinal biomarker.
